ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a common-emitter transistor amplifier circuit, with the power supply terminal marked as +16V; the collector is connected to +16V through resistor RC, the base is biased through RB, the input is coupled to the base through C1, the output is coupled to load RL through C2, the emitter is grounded, and the quiescent collector-emitter voltage UCEQ is marked in the figure. Then reason: When performing DC analysis, C1 and C2 are equivalent to open circuits for DC, so RL does not participate in the DC bias; the emitter is grounded, and the available voltage range of the collector is roughly from 0 to VCC=16V. In order to obtain a suitable quiescent operating point Q, UCEQ is usually taken near the midpoint of the power supply voltage, so that the output signal has a relatively symmetrical swing. Therefore UCEQ ≈ VCC/2 = 16V/2 = 8V.
